subject: Pricing qualification: target $/1M tokens and benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@fintechco.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps: token volumes / target $/1M benchmarking

Hi John — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on pricing and a formal quote: 

1) Volumes you mentioned
- Typical steady-state: ~100M tokens/month
- Peak/target after launch: 150–300M tokens/month (spiky during batch runs)

2) Budget and unit economics
- You said the procurement target is to get to ~ $/1M tokens in a range that makes the feature sustainable for your product team. You gave a broad budget range on the call; can you confirm an expected monthly budget band (e.g., $10k–$50k)?
- For context, teams with similar latency and SLA needs are aiming for $200–$400 per 1M tokens with a mix of reserved capacity + caching.

3) Benchmarking (high level) — rough apples-to-apples numbers we use when qualifying: 
- OpenAI (hosted GPT variants): typically in the $500–$1,200 / 1M tokens range depending on model and context length.
- Anthropic (hosted Claude variants): roughly $400–$900 / 1M tokens for comparable chat models.
- Open-model hosts (managed self-hosting or infra-only providers): wide range, roughly $50–$350 / 1M tokens when you account for infra costs, ops, and lifecycle management — but often with higher operational risk or higher latency.
- Redwood target for this profile (12-month commit + caching + moderate latency SLOs): ~ $250–$350 / 1M tokens. We can push lower with larger committed minimums and dedicated pools.

4) Action items / next steps
- John: please confirm the monthly budget band (best estimate) and whether input tokens are included in your unit-economics view or if you only budget for output tokens.
- Alex: I asked for 2 pricing options to present: (A) Pay-as-you-go (no commit) and (B) Committed reserved (12-mo) with an example quote for 200M tokens/month.
- Dev: can you validate whether our expected caching / prefix strategies can reduce billable tokens by ~10–20% for their patterns?

Attachments: pricing-sheet.pdf (draft example), redwood-benchmark.xlsx (sample perf + cost comparison).

If that all looks right I’ll assemble a short one-pager and an official quote. Appreciate the quick confirm — simple replies work here.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable and economical
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Doe <john.doe@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Recap + next steps: token volumes / target $/1M benchmarking

Thanks Marissa — adding proposed pricing options so we can send a concrete quote tomorrow: 

Option A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- Model family: Redwood-curated open variants (low-latency profile)
- Indicative unit price: $450 / 1M tokens (includes input+output billing)
- No minimums; latency SLOs best-effort

Option B — Committed reserved (12-month)
- Commit: 200M tokens/month (12 month)
- Indicative unit price: $300 / 1M tokens (includes input+output)
- Dedicated pool option (higher upfront & min): $200 / 1M tokens with 12-mo commit + reserved GPU pool (SLA-backed latency targets)

Notes:
- These are benchmarked vs public hosted providers and our internal infra math (GPU utilization, batching, KV cache hit assumptions).
- Reductions assume we can enable prefix caching and a 10–20% effective token reduction for their workload.
- We’ll include a sensitivity table in the quote to show cost at 100/200/300M tokens.

Marissa — when John confirms budget band, I’ll turn this into a formal quote and include the sensitivity table. Dev — can you confirm the 10–20% caching estimate?

—Alex
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0112
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Recap + next steps: token volumes / target $/1M benchmarking

+1 on Alex’s numbers. We can realistically expect 10–18% reduction in billable tokens with prefix/KV caching and some prompt templating. For the 200M token committed profile, we can also enable request-level deduping which helps during batch ingestion windows.

Will add a short cost-sensitivity worksheet to the shared redwood-benchmark.xlsx showing the effective $/1M after caching.

—Dev
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.ai
From: John Doe <john.doe@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: token volumes / target $/1M benchmarking

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and team — thanks for the options. A few clarifying Qs before we loop in procurement: 

1) When you quote $/1M tokens, is that input + output or output-only? We budget differently depending on that.
2) For the committed reserved pricing ($300 / 1M or $200 / 1M dedicated), are there minimum monthly spend commitments? If so, what are the ramp/termination terms?
3) Can you share the benchmark workbook comparing OpenAI/Anthropic/redwood (the redwood-benchmark.xlsx you mentioned) and a one-page cost summary we can circulate internally?

Procurement — looping you in: procurement@fintechco.com. Our target is to close contractual terms this quarter if numbers align.

If you can answer 1–3 we’ll confirm a preferred option and I’ll have procurement request the formal quote/PO template.

Best,
John Doe
VP, Product Engineering | FinTechCo
john.doe@fintechco.com | +1 (617) 555-0220
